differences.what: B states the fixed sizes h=100, v=161700, N=v^3, m=10^6 and the invocation and wire counts I=3v^2=78440670000, W_b=177176569091445000000, W_c=1873807244643542670000; A gives none of these constants or wire counts

differences.what: B's root claim states that the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model; A has no step on the conjecture. Neither gives the liminf argument

items.note: Only B mentions the conclusion, and it does so without the eventual-lower-bound/liminf reasoning.

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: a restored-scratch bank-exchange network, frames, nested labels, s<Wm, eta and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, the two recurrences, the transform layout, resampling and chirp, the algorithm and the cost table. A's chain thins at the label budget: it has no residual table and never establishes the orthonormal residual bases that the complex count s_c relies on. It also only asserts the factorization behind the rank-many interchanges. B carries these links and also states the disproof clause at the root.

errors.says: The layout method moves 'the top slots into a prefix (about dK slot moves)'.
errors.paper: The prefix receives the top slot (i,l-1) of each length-2^l axis and the lowest b=(l-1) mod K slots h=b-1,...,0 of every axis. The latter make up most of the D(b+1)=O(dK) moves.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error; B's only misstatement is a minor slip about which slots form the transform-layout prefix. On core items B carries essential sub-derivations that A lacks: the per-edge residual table, the h-2 side-edge residual and the orthonormal residual bases over F_2 (L1, L2, L4), and the elimination proof of A=E_1 Pi E_2 with the choice of prime (M1, M2). B also adds the network constants and wire counts, the fixed rationals with the layer-condition check, the unequal-width interchange and fuller cost tables. A's few unique details are balanced by others in B.
